newsitem.title: USA: General Mills sales volume soft in March.
newsitem.headline: General Mills sales volume soft in March.

text.p: General Mills Inc on Wednesday said weak sales volume in January and February had extended into the first half of March.

To reach the $3.10-a-share consensus earnings estimate for fiscal 1997, ending in May, the company would have to show fourth-quarter sales volume growth exceeding the four percent growth posted in the year to date, the company added.

"In the fourth quarter, we need to see volume slightly above our nine-month trend line rate to achieve the estimate," Eric Larson, the company's senior vice president for investor relations, told Reuters.

Analysts said that the company indicated during a conference call earlier Wednesday that it was more comfortable with an earnings estimate of $3.05 a share in fiscal 1997, compared with the current consensus of $3.10.
Larson added that "a number of our lines," including cereal, were showing volume weakness.

Earlier, General Mills said domestic retail sales volume for its food products dropped one percent in the fiscal third quarter, ended February 23. Its cereal sales volume was off three percent in the third quarter but rose four percent for the first nine months.
General Mills, the second-largest U.S. cereal maker, said its year-to-date cereal growth outpaced the domestic industry's one percent gain.
"The cereal category continued to be in transition in the quarter," Larson said, adding that the industry overall showed a 0.3 percent drop in sales in the company's third quarter.
That transition involved a drop in the number of promotions after several companies reduced retail prices.
In the fourth quarter, General Mills faces a tough comparison for its cereal volume, Larson said, adding it had both higher prices and higher promotional spending in the year-ago period.

After "very quiet third quarter" for marketing, General Mills plans several promotions during its fourth quarter, Larson said, including the previously announced tie-in with the movie, "The Lost World: Jurassic Park."
